Map the aggregated source data

Source: R/plot_sources.R
plot_sources.Rd

This function draws maps showing, for each source location (e.g. weather station), the mean, the standard deviation and the number of isotopic measurements stored in aggregated source data (as produced by prepsources). Such maps help to explore the source data before fitting the isoscape: e.g. to see where sources are, which areas are poorly covered, which locations rely on few measurements, or which values look unusual.

Usage

plot_sources(
  data,
  which = c("mean", "sd", "n"),
  labels = FALSE,
  points = list(pch = 21, cex = 1, lwd = 0.5, col = "black", digits = 1),
  borders = list(borders = NA, lwd = 0.5, col = "darkgrey"),
  palette = list(step = NA, range = c(NA, NA), n_labels = 11, digits = 2, fn = NA),
  plot = TRUE,
  ask = length(which) > 1 && grDevices::dev.interactive()
)

Arguments

data

A dataframe containing aggregated source data, as produced by prepsources (without splitting the data, i.e. with a single row per source location)

which

A vector of strings indicating which statistics to map, among "mean" (mean of the isotopic values), "sd" (standard deviation of the isotopic values) and "n" (number of measurements). By default, all three are mapped, one after the other.

labels

A logical indicating whether the values should be written on the maps instead of being represented by coloured points (default = FALSE)

points

A list containing information for the display of the points or labels (see details)

borders

A list containing information for the display of borders (see details)

palette

A list containing information for the display of the colours (see details)

plot

A logical indicating whether the maps should be drawn (default = TRUE); if FALSE, the maps are only returned

ask

A logical indicating whether the user should be asked to press before each new map. By default, this is the case when several maps are drawn on an interactive graphic device.

Value

A named list of maps (objects of class trellis, one per statistic), returned invisibly. Each map can be drawn again using print.

Details

Each statistic is shown on its own map. When several maps are drawn in an interactive session, you are asked to press before each new map (as for plot() called on the output of stats::lm); see the argument ask. By default, the value of each source location is represented by the colour of a point (see the colour key on the right side of each map). For datasets containing few source locations, you can instead write the values on the maps by setting labels = TRUE.

The arguments points, borders and palette are lists which can be used to fine-tune the maps, in the same way as for the other plotting functions of IsoriX (see plots). The argument points controls the display of the points (pch, cex, lwd, and col for the colour of their outline) or of the labels (cex, col and digits for the number of decimals). The argument borders controls the display of the borders (borders, lwd, col): by default, the country borders provided with IsoriX (CountryBorders) are drawn, use borders = list(borders = NULL) to draw none. The argument palette controls the colours (fn, step, range, n_labels, digits), as for plot.ISOSCAPE; each map uses its own colour scale.

Source locations straddling the International Date Line are drawn on a continuous map (e.g. from 70 to 210 degrees of longitude).

See also

prepsources for the function aggregating the source data

plots for the other plotting functions of IsoriX

Examples


## The examples below will only be run if sufficient time is allowed
## You can change that by typing e.g. options_IsoriX(example_maxtime = XX)
## if you want to allow for examples taking up to ca. XX seconds to run
## (so don't write XX but put a number instead!)

if (getOption_IsoriX("example_maxtime") > 10) {
  ## Aggregate the source data for Germany
  GNIPDataDEagg <- prepsources(data = GNIPDataDE)

  ## Map the mean, standard deviation and number of measurements
  plot_sources(GNIPDataDEagg)

  ## Same, writing the values instead (better for few source locations)
  plot_sources(GNIPDataDEagg, labels = TRUE)

  ## Map only the number of measurements, with another palette
  plot_sources(GNIPDataDEagg, which = "n", palette = list(fn = NULL))

  ## Map the means for the European data
  plot_sources(GNIPDataEUagg, which = "mean")
}
